name: Construction
title: Design change and site impact coordination
summary: Trace a design revision through quantities, procurement, and site sequencing before project teams approve a change.
situation: Illustrative architecture: A commercial building project receives a revised mechanical layout after installation has begun. The contractor needs to identify affected work packages, material orders, and coordination questions. Agents prepare change evidence and scenarios; licensed designers and authorized project managers retain technical and commercial decisions.
problem: Drawings, building models, requests for information, and purchase orders use different identifiers and revision conventions. A generated summary can overlook installed work or treat an unapproved sketch as the governing design, creating rework and contractual confusion.
whyAgents: Revision, quantity, schedule, and procurement specialists examine distinct dependencies. Model comparison and quantity calculation services provide deterministic evidence while agents draft questions and explain bounded schedule scenarios.
outcome: The intended result is a reviewable operational decision with source evidence and explicit ownership. Evaluate review preparation and missed dependencies before claiming reduced project delay. Construction outcomes depend on design resolution, site execution, and commercial agreement; the agent system should expose those dependencies rather than obscure them.

agents.name: Revision investigator
agents.responsibility: Compare approved drawing and model revisions and identify changed elements.
agents.boundary: Cannot approve design changes or treat draft drawings as issued instructions.

agents.name: Quantity impact agent
agents.responsibility: Map changed elements to measured quantities and installed-work records.
agents.boundary: Cannot certify payment quantities or structural adequacy.

agents.name: Sequence planner
agents.responsibility: Evaluate work-package dependencies and access conflicts around the change.
agents.boundary: Cannot authorize unsafe sequencing or alter the contractual baseline.

agents.name: Commercial evidence agent
agents.responsibility: Retrieve affected orders and draft requests for clarification or change review.
agents.boundary: Cannot accept claims, agree prices, or issue subcontract instructions.

systems.name: Common data environment
systems.role: Controls model and drawing revisions, issue status, and project permissions.

systems.name: Project controls platform
systems.role: Owns schedules, work packages, progress evidence, and authorized change records.

systems.name: Procurement and site systems
systems.role: Provide committed orders, installation observations, and accountable field confirmations.

flow.title: Register issued revision
flow.description: Verify the document's issue status, project scope, and superseded revision before opening a change investigation.

flow.title: Compare design elements
flow.description: Run governed model or drawing comparisons and retain element identifiers and view references for human inspection.

flow.title: Map physical progress
flow.description: Join changed elements to installed quantities and active work packages, flagging unverified site reports.

flow.title: Evaluate consequences
flow.description: Calculate quantity deltas and bounded schedule scenarios, separating confirmed procurement commitments from estimates.

flow.title: Prepare coordinated review
flow.description: Present design questions, site conflicts, affected orders, and scenario assumptions to design and project-control owners.

flow.title: Publish authorized actions
flow.description: Record approved instructions through established project channels and track acknowledgement by each affected subcontractor or supplier.

diagrams.caption: A draft sketch is mistaken for an issued revision. The workflow records unresolved work and resumes only after the source state and reviewer authority are checked.

failures.scenario: A draft sketch is mistaken for an issued revision.
failures.detection: Document status and transmittal checks show it lacks approved issue authority.
failures.recovery: Quarantine it as discussion evidence and prevent downstream instruction generation.

failures.scenario: Site progress reports conflict with installed-work photographs.
failures.detection: Element timestamps and field verification records disagree.
failures.recovery: Request a current field check and keep quantity and schedule consequences provisional.

controls: Require issued-document status and revision lineage before treating design information as authoritative.
Preserve licensed designer approval for technical design and safety decisions.
Keep contract notices and commercial commitments behind project-manager authorization.
Record quantity units and model element identifiers for every calculated delta.
Enforce project and subcontract access boundaries in drawings and cost records.

metrics.name: Impact packet latency
metrics.definition: Time from accepted revision to a coordinated review packet with affected work references.

metrics.name: Element traceability
metrics.definition: Reported impacts linked to governed model or drawing elements divided by reported impacts.

metrics.name: Field verification coverage
metrics.definition: Affected installed-work items supported by current verified site evidence divided by affected installed items.

metrics.name: Acknowledgement completeness
metrics.definition: Approved instructions acknowledged by every required recipient divided by issued instruction sets.

tradeoffs.benefit: Makes revision effects inspectable at element level.
tradeoffs.cost: Older drawings and inconsistent identifiers require manual mapping.

tradeoffs.benefit: Show possible sequencing consequences before commitment.
tradeoffs.cost: Assumptions about productivity and access require field validation.
Coordination can take longer when approvals are interdependent.

rollout.acceptance: Project teams verify issued status, element mapping, quantity units, and installed-work contradictions.
One work package receives draft impact packets without contractual instructions or baseline changes.
Approved actions enter existing registers after superseded-document and missing-acknowledgement tests pass.
